chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Najm ibn Huteym Al-Ghanawy, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Despair of what is in the hands of the people is the honor of the Believer in his religion. Or have you not heard the words of Hatim: 'When you determine upon despair (from the people), you find richness when you recognize the self; and greed is poverty.'

key_terms.النَّفَسَ: The self or soul (in the context of self-recognition/contentment)
key_terms.الْيَأْسُ: Despair or giving up hope (specifically from others' wealth)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of despairing from people's wealth in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'ya's' not as hopelessness, but as the conscious detachment from seeking worldly sustenance from people, thereby securing spiritual dignity (izzah). This concept is reinforced by the pre-Islamic poet Hatim al-Tai, whose verse illustrates that renouncing desire for others' wealth leads to inner richness, while greed constitutes true poverty. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for the Shia ethical principle of 'ghina al-nafs' (self-sufficiency), distinguishing between material need and spiritual independence.
